title: Export Sector Status to FEVM
description: Exports three new methods — ValidateSectorStatus, GenerateSectorLocation, and GetNominalSectorExpiration — from the builtin miner actor, allowing FEVM smart contracts to query the liveness status (Active/Faulty/Dead) and expiration of Filecoin sectors, laying the foundation for programmable storage applications.

storageProviders: Storage providers can integrate with FEVM contracts for real-time sector status monitoring and smart contract-based storage coordination.
This proposal only adds read-only view methods to the miner actor — it does not affect existing workflows, proof-of-power, or block production logic.
Enables new use cases such as custom storage payments, bad-bit insurance systems, and markets for sector repair built on smart contracts.
clients: Decentralized applications can verify sector status directly on-chain without relying on centralized indexing services to confirm data availability.
Combined with FIP-0109's sector commitment notifications, clients gain full on-chain visibility into the sector lifecycle from creation to termination.
tokenHolders: No direct impact on FIL token economics or supply, but the proposal indirectly benefits network value by enabling a richer programmable storage ecosystem.
applicationDevelopers: Developers can build FEVM contracts that react to sector state changes (Active/Faulty/Dead), enabling custom markets, data availability verification, and other advanced use cases.

ValidateSectorStatus uses a validating interface (pass in status, returns true/false) rather than a data retrieval interface, intentionally placing the index search burden on off-chain callers to allow future miner actor evolution.

GenerateSectorLocation is designed for off-chain calls, performing an expensive linear search to locate a sector's deadline and partition index; on-chain ValidateSectorStatus calls require only lightweight validation.
GetNominalSectorExpiration provides a convenient query for sector expiration epochs. Note: early termination can invalidate this value, so it serves only as a hint.
